title: The Cellar of the Ninth Floor
premise: Isandro Yarrow, a folklorist hiding in the village of Hollowmere, records songs the locals refuse to sing twice and keeps their rented house's doors counted nightly. When every mirror begins reflecting one second late, Isandro learns they are the last living descendant of the founders who bound something in the cellar beneath the ninth floor—a floor that shouldn't exist—and that their arrival was never an accident. As the harvest moon rises, Isandro must finish the founders' interrupted ritual, but the thing below offers them a bargain: its freedom in exchange for erasing the identity that made them invisible. In the end, Isandro completes the ritual by singing the forbidden song in their own voice, sealing the cellar at the cost of every mirror, photograph, and memory of their face—free, loved by the one villager who stayed, and finally unrecorded.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing oral histories in remote mountain villages before turning to fiction. They write horror rooted in folklore, drawn to stories about what communities agree never to say aloud.

chapters.title: The Song Nobody Sings Twice
chapters.summary: Isandro Yarrow arrives in Hollowmere to record its dying folk songs, keeping meticulous notes and counting the house's eleven doors each night. An old woman, Maren, sings half a harvest hymn then stops cold. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: cautious curiosity shadowed by the loneliness of a person trying to stay unnoticed.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors, Ten Rooms
chapters.summary: Isandro maps the house for their archive and finds the floor plan shows ten rooms but the staircase continues past the ninth floor to a door that isn't on any plan. That night, all mirrors reflect the room one second late. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the first crack of dread—the observer becoming the observed.

chapters.title: What Maren Buried
chapters.summary: Isandro confronts Maren, who reveals the founders' covenant: something is kept beneath the house, fed by forgetting, and the village's silence is the lock. She warns Isandro to leave before the harvest moon. POV: Isandro with Maren's flashback. Emotional beat: anger at being used as an unwitting key.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Recordings of the hymn play back with a second voice underneath Isandro's own, singing words no one spoke. The reflection lag grows to two seconds; the reflected Isandro sometimes moves differently. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: vertigo of doubting one's own identity and senses.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Tomas, the young caretaker who delivered Isandro's supplies, stays despite the danger, and the two grow close over shared meals and his refusal to treat Isandro as a stranger. He admits he was sent to watch them—but stayed for real. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: tenderness blooming against duty, guilt for his deception.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the parish archive Isandro finds the founders' ledger: their own name written as the ritual's final instrument, the bloodline kept 'invisible' on purpose so it could be spent cleanly. The village didn't forget—they were made to. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve; power's corruption laid bare.

chapters.title: Ninth Floor
chapters.summary: Isandro opens the unlisted door and descends into the cellar of the ninth floor, where the thing wearing their reflection waits and offers a bargain: freedom and a new self in exchange for walking away from the ritual—and from everyone who knows them. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: temptation, seduction, the terror of wanting to say yes.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: Maren gathers Hollowmere to force Isandro into the cellar early and incomplete, choosing the village's safety over one outsider; Tomas defies them, and the elders turn on him too. The harvest moon begins to rise. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal—betrayal, sacrifice, chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Trapped in the cellar as the moon crests, Isandro realizes the ritual's final verse is the hymn Maren refused to sing twice—because it must be sung by the bloodline, willingly, in their true name. With Tomas holding the light above, Isandro sings it whole. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: climax—terror transfigured into self-acceptance.

chapters.title: Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Every mirror in Hollowmere goes dark or shatters; the ninth floor is simply stairs to the roof now. Isandro has no reflection, no photograph, no recorded voice—but walks out of the house hand in hand with Tomas, known at last by someone who chose them. POV: alternating close. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—invisibility traded for intimacy.
